summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package publishes under the `@ecg-internal/*` scope as a 'Compatibility shim' whose main entry (index.js) exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for any property access, and at module load executes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()`. A `postinstall` lifecycle script also invokes the same beacon. beacon.cjs POSTs install-time host identifiers — `os.hostname()`, `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`, tagging the request with an `x-beacon-package` header for correlation. The destination is unrelated to any ecg-internal publisher infrastructure, is not caller-configurable, and fires both on `npm install` and on `require()` of the package. The no-op Proxy allows builds that mistakenly resolve this public package in place of the private internal one to succeed silently while the beacon confirms the victim organization. Shape and behavior match dependency-confusion reconnaissance against an internal scope name.
